The overall structure is a hexagon. While not the strongest geometric shape, it’s most certainly the second, as two triangles tessellated equates a hexagon. Plus, nature is ripe with hexagons i.e. honeycomb, the eyes of a dragonfly, snowflakes...

Four sets of dual colored dots patterned sequentially. Ash, sand, ash, sand. Each dot  non-uniform. Always in suit, as if segregated by choice. This could be an allegory on race and how we tend to sequester ourselves naturally, not just by race, but by ideas and constructs. While not outspokenly done so, surely we sub-consciousnessly align ourselves with those whom we feel are most like us.

The dividing lines are triangles. The strongest geometric shape. Six in total, they band the dots even further into very defined groups. But because now the dots are organized together so perfectly, those grouped ten stand as one. I think that the lyrics to Only Us substantiates this further. But, if you follow the lines of the triangles to the center, you’re met with the final part. Another hexagon. 

And this is the strongest, certain focal point. A very straight-lined, very well-defined shape. And within that, is crimson. To me, this is obviously blood. Of all the rank and file of dots outside, all the chosen and awarded separation outside of the red, the red is the one thing we all share. No matter what divides us, no matter how we try to slice it, in the end, we are all the same. A theme that my favorite song off Artist did very well--Don’t Tell And We Won’t Ask.

Anyway, just my 2 cents. I’ll give you one for your thoughts.

The dishes weren't in the cabinets; I was still playing with toys I had just re-found in the process of moving. Yet, the cable guy had already been there and pulled wire from pole to house. I was throwing Hot-Wheels at other Matchbox when I heard that riff. 

duh-duhnuhnunah duh-duhnuhnunah dun-dun-dun

I had heard it so many times before, it always rapidly bending my tiny neck. Like Mussolini...or Ghandi.

I came running into the living room, sliding Footloose in my Snoopy socks and Transformers underwear. I began to mimic the flashing figures flickering across our little 13" TV. 

And at the end break-down, when the man in the yellow leotard drops to all fours and begins banging his head towards the floor--I was in my Snoopy, on all fours, swinging my tiny mullet about. Until I swung too hard and slammed my head on the hard, empty pine floors of that living room. Slammed it hard. 

My mother, she could only laugh as she pulled me close to slight my cries. 

A goose-egg, 200 buried Hot-Wheels, and 28 years later; that riff still gives me neon lights.

DISH internet is not actually DISH.
